Title: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel prices rise from tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The retail prices of RON97 petrol and unsubsidised RON95 petrol will increase by 20 sen per litre each, while unsubsidised diesel will rise by 15 sen per litre from Sept 24 to 30.
The Finance Ministry (MOF) said the new prices would be RM5.05 per litre for RON97, RM4.57 per litre for unsubsidised RON95 and RM5.42 per litre for unsubsidised diesel.
It said continued supply constraints on refined petroleum products had kept market prices elevated.
"Disruptions to refined petroleum production in Russia, one of the world's largest diesel exporters, have further intensified the situation.
"Diesel exports from the Middle East also fell by more than 50 per cent between March and August 2026," it said in a statement today.
MOF said the recovery of global refining capacity was important to stabilise petroleum product prices, while the resumption of petroleum flows through the Strait of Hormuz could help ease pressure on crude oil and refined petroleum product prices.
However, it said global geopolitical uncertainties were expected to continue influencing petroleum price fluctuations in the medium term, with potential conflicts posing risks of significantly higher oil transportation costs.
"Supertanker rental rates for several routes from the Middle East have reached record levels of about US$1 million per day following shipping disruptions," it said.
Meanwhile, MOF said the government would continue protecting the people and businesses from the impact of global uncertainties by maintaining targeted subsidies through Budi Madani, Budi Diesel, the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS).
The ministry said fuel supplies in the country remained sufficient, but urged consumers to use fuel prudently, plan journeys efficiently and reduce unnecessary travel to help conserve supplies and manage subsidy expenditure.
"The government will continue to adopt a prudent approach to cushion the impact of price fluctuations while ensuring the country's fuel supply remains sufficient and secure," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PH to announce candidates one to two weeks before nomination
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Pakatan Harapan is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election one to two weeks before nomination day, said the Prime Minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin.
He said the move would allow PH to make early preparations instead of waiting until the last minute to finalise its candidates.
"This time, we are better prepared to name our candidates," he told reporters after visiting beneficiaries of the Ziarah Kasih programme at the Kuala Linggi state constituency.
Azman said the candidate selection process would be left to the party leadership, taking into account lists submitted by party divisions, state leaders and the grassroots before the final decision is made.
Earlier, Azman visited seven recipients of the Ziarah Kasih programme, including a single mother with two children who is unable to work after being involved in a road accident.
The programme also provided cash assistance from the Prime Minister's Department, as well as follow-up aid such as wheelchairs or other support where required and eligible.
Azman said the Ziarah Kasih programme was among the activities carried out by the Political Secretary's Office and would continue in several other areas in Melaka, including the Jasin parliamentary constituency next week.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Brazilian singer, 4 others killed in helicopter crash
Article:
SAO PAULO:  Five people, including Brazilian singer Rick Sollo of the sertanejo music duo Rick & Renner, were found dead Tuesday after their helicopter crashed in a mountainous area of southern Brazil's Santa Catarina state, the fire department said, Xinhua reported.
The helicopter went missing on Monday after taking off from Porto Belo on the state's northern coast bound for Sao Joaquim, where severe weather and thunderstorms had been forecast.
Also aboard were businessman Bruno Avelar, cameraman Paulo Soares, the pilot and co-pilot.
The wreckage was located Tuesday during a search involving about 40 firefighters, more than 10 vehicles and drones, two search dogs and an aircraft amid foggy conditions.
Brazil's civil aviation agency said the aircraft, a Bell 430 manufactured in 2001, was authorised to operate.
Rick & Renner is one of Brazil's most well-known sertanejo music duos with a career dating back to the 1980s. — BERNAMA- XINHUA

Title: Teacher-student scandal exposed after hotel visits, video recording
Article:
SERDANG: A female teacher's alleged inappropriate relationship with her 17-year-old male student came to light after his family and school authorities discovered a video involving the two.
The relationship is believed to have started last year, with the pair allegedly checking into hotels in Seri Kembangan several times and meeting at the teacher's home.
A source told Harian Metro that the student claimed the teacher initially invited him to go out for a walk and a meal before taking him to a hotel in Seri Kembangan.
The source said the teacher allegedly engaged in sexual acts with the student and recorded them on her mobile phone.
"The incident happened several times, including at the suspect's home.
"However, the matter came to light on Monday after the family and school authorities became aware of it, including discovering the recorded video," the source was quoted as saying by Harian Metro.
Following this, the student and school authorities are believed to have lodged police reports for further action.
The source said police subsequently arrested the teacher in the Bandar Kinrara area at about 10.30pm on Monday.
The case is being investigated under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
The New Straits Times has reached out to Serdang police.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Agriculture Ministry denies mandatory 20pc padi deduction rate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The agriculture and food security ministry has refuted claims that a mandatory minimum deduction rate of 20 per cent has been imposed on padi sold by farmers.
The ministry said deduction rates depended strictly on the physical condition and quality of the padi at the time of sale.
"Padi delivered at optimum quality will attract significantly lower deduction rates in accordance with established standards.
"To ensure transparency and prevent misconduct, the ministry, through the state-level Padi and Rice Regulatory Section, initiated nationwide special monitoring operations on padi grading on Sept 14," it said in a statement.
The ministry said the move followed ongoing harvesting seasons in several states, with monitoring operations to be expanded to other states scheduled to begin harvesting soon.
"The measures aim to ensure all rice mills comply with grading procedures transparently, fairly and with integrity," it said.
The ministry was responding to an Utusan Malaysia report published on Sept 21 on farmers' concerns over high deduction rates.
It added that excessively high deduction rates not only hurt farmers' incomes but also risk disrupting the broader national paddy and rice ecosystem.
"To ensure fair weighing processes, quality assessments at licensed padi buyers or commercial rice mills are strictly calculated based on physical quality parameters—including moisture content, immature grain, damaged grain, and foreign matter content," it said.
Since 2017, the ministry has enforced the standard operating procedure (SOP) for padi grading under the Padi Specification and Grading Standard (MS 84:2017) at all mills, including Bernas and private operators.
"Adherence to this uniform SOP protects farmers from unfair practices, ensures they receive accurate padi price subsidies based on net yield, and prevents public funds leakage," it said.
The ministry said strengthening the local rice industry required the continued commitment of all stakeholders in the ecosystem, reaffirming its priority to safeguard farmers' welfare and national food security.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MNRB's FY26 final dividend at 15 sen per share
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MNRB Holdings Bhd has declared a final dividend of 15 sen per share for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, with one-third of the payout eligible for reinvestment under its dividend reinvestment plan (DRP).
In a bourse filing, the company said five sen per share, or 33.3 per cent of the final dividend, will be subject to the DRP.
Under the plan, shareholders may choose to receive the entire dividend in cash, reinvest the full eligible portion into new MNRB shares and receive the balance in cash, or reinvest part of the eligible portion and receive the remainder in cash.
It said the issue price of the new shares to be issued under the DRP, as well as the book closure and dividend payment dates, will be announced later.
The authority for the company to issue new shares under the DRP was approved by shareholders at the company's annual general meeting on Sept 26, 2025.
The DRP itself was approved by shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting on Sept 25, 2019.
MNRB said it will apply to Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd for the listing and quotation of the new shares to be issued under the DRP on the Main Market.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tourism Malaysia seeks bigger 2027 Budget allocation to hit 47mil arrivals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tourism Malaysia is seeking a higher allocation under Budget 2027 to help achieve its target of 47 million international tourist arrivals under the Visit Malaysia campaign, which has been extended until 2027.
Its director-general, Mohd Amirul Rizal Abdul Rahim, said the additional allocation was important to sustain Malaysia's promotion in international markets and ensure the country remained competitive in attracting tourists.
He said the request also took into account the views of tourism industry players, who hoped allocations for the sector could be increased to strengthen efforts to promote Malaysia globally.
"The hope of industry players is certainly that the allocation can be increased. To remain competitive, we need an injection, not only financially but also through collaboration with tourism industry players," he said when met after the launch of the Edu+ 2.0 Education Tourism Package, EatVenture and Taste of Orchard Package in conjunction with the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign at Saloma Kuala Lumpur here today.
He said the tourism sector had a wide spillover effect on various groups in society, benefiting not only hotels and restaurants but also operators of tourism-related products and services.
Mohd Amirul Rizal said the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry (Motac) had requested a higher allocation than last year to ensure the sector remained resilient, including through the organisation of international-scale events.
"International-scale events do not necessarily have to be large, but they can attract foreign tourists to come to Malaysia specifically to attend the event. That's what we are trying to do," he said, stressing that the tourism sector also made a significant contribution to the country's gross domestic product (GDP).
On tourism performance, he said international visitor arrivals increased by 2.5 per cent to 21.1 million between January and June this year, compared with 20.6 million in the same period last year.
Meanwhile, domestic tourism expenditure in the first quarter increased by 15.8 per cent to RM34 billion from RM29.4 billion in the same period last year, while the number of domestic visitors rose by 7.2 per cent to 74.7 million from 69.7 million.
He said the figures showed positive growth, but the sector had yet to reach the target set under the Visit Malaysia campaign, partly due to the impact of the Middle East conflict that began in early March.
However, he said the government remained committed to the target of 47 million international tourist arrivals to maintain the promotional momentum despite external factors such as geopolitical conflicts.
"It is important for this year that we continue to create demand, which is why the Prime Minister agreed to extend the Visit Malaysia campaign until 2027," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aneka Jaringan bags RM26mil serviced apartment works
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Aneka Jaringan Holdings Bhd's unit Aneka Jaringan Sdn Bhd (AJSB) has bagged a RM26.2 million contract for earthworks, piling and substructure works for a high-rise serviced apartment development in Jalan Yap Kwan Seng, Kuala Lumpur.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said AJSB received the letter of award from WDA Architects Sdn Bhd, acting on behalf of developer Exsim YKS 54 Sdn Bhd.
The contract involves earthworks, piling and pile caps, retaining walls and sub-structure works for a 53-storey serviced apartment development.
The project will comprise 394 serviced apartment units across 45 floors, from levels six to 50, along with mechanical and electrical facilities, public amenities, a strata office and mechanically operated car parks spanning the lower ground to level 16.
The contract started on Sept 15, and is scheduled for completion on Aug 14, 2028.
Aneka Jaringan said the commencement date was agreed during the final contract negotiations to ensure delivery of the works would not be delayed.
The company expects the contract to contribute positively to its consolidated earnings and net assets for the financial years ending Aug 31, 2027 and Aug 31, 2028.

Title: Rimbunan Sawit takes RM10mil hit from blockade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rimbunan Sawit Bhd estimates a revenue shortfall of about RM10 million following a three-month disruption at its Ulu Teru Estate in Miri, caused by a blockade of the estate's main access route.
The Sarawak-based plantation group said the blockade, which disrupted access since June 18, was lifted on Sept 15 with estate operations fully resuming on Sept 21.
"The board will continue to monitor the situation and management will take the necessary measures to safeguard the company's operations and interests," it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
Ulu Teru Estate is operated by PJP Pelita Ulu Teru Plantation Sdn Bhd, which is 60 per cent-owned by Nescaya Palma Sdn Bhd.
The latter is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Rimbunan Sawit.
The estate covers about 7,900 hectares (ha), or roughly 13 per cent of Rimbunan Sawit's total plantation land bank of 61,120ha in Sarawak.
The company previously said on July 6 that the disruption had affected harvesting activities, transportation of fresh fruit bunches and certain other estate operations.
Rimbunan Sawit did not disclose the reason for the blockade in its latest filing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RoS asks PN to explain why it should not be deregistered
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional yesterday received a notice from the Registrar of Societies (RoS) seeking an explanation as to why the coalition should not be deregistered within 30 days.
A source confirmed to Berita Harian that the notice had been sent to the PN chairman, secretary-general and all PN component parties yesterday.
"Yes, I can confirm that this is accurate, but I am not sure to whom the RoS notice was handed, whether the chairman or secretary-general.
"I was informed that the secretary-general will also issue a statement on the matter," the source said as quoted by BH.
It is understood that the notice also includes an instruction for several PN component parties not to use the coalition's logo in any activities until the RoS makes a final decision.
The New Straits Times have reached out to RoS.
However, it is understood that the agency will issue an official statement.
The RoS had previously confirmed receiving an official complaint from Bersatu on Aug 11 against PN.
The complaint included claims that Bersatu was not involved in a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16 and questions over the party's membership status in the coalition.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin
on Saturday urged the RoS to make an immediate decision on the complaint, which also alleged that PN leaders had breached eight provisions.
He said Bersatu had raised eight key matters which it claimed had been violated or disregarded by PN leaders.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two schoolgirls injured after being hit by motorcycle in Permatang Pauh
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH: Two schoolgirls were injured after being hit by a motorcycle while crossing a road in front of their school this morning.
The incident occurred at about 7.20am as the girls, aged eight and nine, were crossing a pedestrian crossing while on their way to school.
Seberang Prai Tengah district police chief Assistant Commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said police had detected a 30-second video of the incident circulating on social media.
"Preliminary investigations found that the two pupils were crossing the pedestrian crossing before being hit by a motorcycle ridden by an unidentified individual," he said.
Both pupils suffered minor injuries and received treatment.
Nik Aminuddin said police were investigating to identify the motorcyclist and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.
The case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Police urged anyone with information to contact the nearest police station or investigating officer Inspector Hafizi Mansor at 017-566 0103.
Nik Aminuddin reminded motorists to slow down, comply with traffic regulations and give way to pedestrians, particularly around schools and pedestrian crossings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three foreign students held over suspected murder in Ipoh
Article:
IPOH: Police have detained three foreign students over the suspected murder of a local man in Kampung Kuchai here on Sept 18.
Ipoh police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the three suspects, aged between 17 and 20, were arrested at their apartment this morning.
He said the 53-year-old victim was found unconscious by members of the public in an open area, lying on the ground with injuries to his face.
"The victim was then taken to Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital here for further treatment, but after receiving treatment several times, he was pronounced dead around  6.42pm yesterday.
"An autopsy found that the cause of death was blunt force trauma to the head," he said in a statement.
Najib said police subsequently arrested the three suspects as part of investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
He said police were still conducting further investigations to determine the actual motive for the incident and the relationship between the victim and suspects.
"Anyone with information about the incident is urged to assist investigations by contacting the Ipoh district police headquarters at 05-2451500 or any nearby police station," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two Mandiri-linked individuals remanded three days over money laundering probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two individuals linked to non-governmental organisation (NGO) Mandiri have been remanded for three days to assist investigations under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA).
The remand order against both men began today.
The remand application was understood to have been heard at the Jinjang Central Lock-up in Kuala Lumpur.
Amir Hariri Abdul Hadi and Dobby Chew, who is director of Mandiri Development Centre Sdn Bhd, were detained by the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department's Anti-Money Laundering Investigation Team (AMLA) yesterday.
They were detained at 3.53pm to assist investigations under Section 4(1) of AMLATFPUAA 2001.
The arrests followed an investigation paper opened on Sept 10 concerning the receipt of funds suspected to be proceeds from unlawful activities between 2024 and 2026.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail was quoted as saying that police would conduct a thorough investigation in accordance with the law against any parties suspected of being linked to the case.
He said the investigation included the storage, transfer, use and deposit or withdrawal of money suspected to be linked to proceeds from unlawful activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Auku replacement Bill expected to be tabled in December – Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The first reading of the Bill that will replace the Universities and University Colleges Act (Auku) is expected to be tabled at the Dewan Rakyat sitting in December, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
He said the ministry was working to complete a comprehensive series of engagements with stakeholders to ensure the Bill took into account the entire national higher education ecosystem before it was tabled in parliament.
"In terms of the timeline, we will try to see whether we can carry out the first reading, perhaps at the December parliamentary sitting.
"But you must remember, it (the Bill) will involve very extensive engagement," he said after the closing ceremony of the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit (URIIS) 2026 here today.
He added that the draft Bill was not confined to student freedom, but also covered administrative structures, university governance and academic matters.
He explained that Auku contains 44 sections, seven of which involve students, while the rest cover matters related to the establishment of universities, university governance, academic matters and others.
"We understand that when drafting a new Act, we must take into account the entire ecosystem of the national higher education system," he said.
Zambry said the latest series of engagements was held with the Parliamentary Special Select Committee to obtain feedback from both government and Opposition representatives.
Meanwhile, turning to Budget 2027, Zambry expressed hope that the ministry would receive a larger allocation to support the Malaysian Higher Education Development Plan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN to decide on Melaka polls cooperation soon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional will soon decide whether to cooperate with other political parties for the 16th Melaka state election.
BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir said the decision would be made after discussions with its top leadership in Melaka.
"BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will make the decision after discussions are held. Our focus at present is on the formal election process.
"A decision on the cooperation will be made soon," he told reporters after the closing ceremony of the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit (URIIS) 2026 here today.
Yesterday, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh
announced the dissolution
of the Melaka Legislative Assembly, effective today.
[[nid:1539542]]
The dissolution paves the way for the 16th Melaka state election. The state assembly has 28 seats, while the current state government's mandate is scheduled to end on Dec 27.
In the 15th Melaka state election on Nov 20, 2021, BN formed the state government after winning 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan won five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.

Title: Melaka election postal voting applications open
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Applications for all categories of domestic and overseas postal voting for the 16th Melaka election opened today.
Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said all applications must be submitted online via the MySPR portal, with the closing date to be announced later.
"Eligible voters who intend to cast their ballots by post must register for or have an existing MySPR account before submitting their application," he said in a statement today.
Khairul Shahril said Category 1A applications covered police and military personnel, election officials, EC members and staff, as well as media personnel.
Applications are also open under Category 1B for Malaysians residing abroad and Category 1C for agencies or organisations.
For further enquiries, applicants can contact the EC hotline at 03-8892 7080 or email upup@spr.gov.my.
Yesterday, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced the dissolution of the Melaka Legislative Assembly, effective today, paving the way for the 16th Melaka election following the consent of Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
Melaka Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum also submitted the dissolution notice to the EC yesterday.
In the 2021 Melaka election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats to form the state government with a more than two-thirds majority, while Pakatan Harapan secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Search for missing fireman in Nepal: Hani prays for closure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The wife of senior fire officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, who remains missing after flash floods struck Nepal, said she has come to terms with whatever fate awaits her husband.
Hani Othman said she and her family had resigned themselves to fate after 29 days of enduring a deeply trying period.
"Whatever fate God has for my husband, whether he returns to our family or returns to his creator, my family and I accept it.
"My hope now is for the best possible outcome for my husband and peace for our family. If permitted by God, I will return to Nepal. I will continue what my husband was doing before this," she said.
Hani had travelled to Kathmandu on her own initiative to seek updates on the search for her husband and members of his group who remained untraceable following the disaster.
While there, she shared regular updates on her efforts to locate her husband and other Malaysians, including visiting hospitals in Nepal to assist with body identification and distributing aid to victims alongside local non-governmental organisations.
Fakhrul, also known as Loe, was reported missing after the four-wheel-drive carrying his Everest Base Camp expedition group along the Tibet route was believed to have been swept away by massive floods and landslides in a valley in Rasuwa.
A total of 55 Malaysians were reported missing following the Aug 26 disaster.
Hani said since returning to Malaysia on Sept 12, she had continued gathering information about her husband through his personal computer, old phone and documents.
"To calm myself, I spend time performing prayers, reading the Quran and listening to lectures on YouTube. I have also received various forms of support from family and friends," she said.
Asked what she hoped for, Hani said she wanted a definitive answer about her husband's fate.
"Having been there for 15 days, I fully understand the situation and the challenges faced by the government. Although I know that only God can help in this situation, I hope the search efforts continue where possible. There will be no results without physical effort," she said.
Hani also urged other affected families to continue praying, remain strong and accept God's decree.
"I deeply understand how heavy these days are for them. No words are comforting enough to erase this yearning and grief.
"May we all be granted extraordinary patience by God to remain resilient through this trial. God willing, we can endure this test together," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rehda asks for special Home Ownership Campaign targeted at unsold completed units for 2027 budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Malaysia has called on the government to introduce a special Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) next year to tackle the issue of existing unsold completed residential units.
This campaign would specifically target unsold completed units that have received a certificate of completion and compliance (CCC).
The association notes that while the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035 aims to improve the alignment of supply and demand through data-driven planning, immediate intervention is necessary to absorb current unsold stock.
A special HOC would complement long-term reforms, improve market liquidity, and enable capital to be recycled into new developments, the association said in its 2027 budget wishlist released today.
The association also highlighted that while many prospective buyers may have the capacity to service monthly repayments, upfront acquisition costs remain a hurdle, as they may face difficulty accumulating sufficient savings for stamp duty and other charges and fees.
Recognizing this challenge to prospective home buyers, Rehda suggested extending the current stamp duty relief to residential properties priced above RM500,000 and up to RM1 million, through an appropriate tiered relief mechanism for purchases made between January and December 2027.
In addition to that, access to end-financing is also identified as a major barrier, especially for young Malaysians, the self-employed, gig-economy workers, and those with variable or non-traditional incomes, noted Rehda.
The association proposed expanding and enhancing the Skim Jaminan Kredit Perumahan (SJKP) and other government-backed housing financing or guarantee mechanisms.
Furthermore, the association suggested improving step-up financing structures that offer lower repayments during the initial years of homeownership.
Rehda also emphasized that housing affordability is affected by the cost of developing and delivering homes, not just purchasers' access to financing.
Rising infrastructure, utility, statutory, regulatory, and compliance costs cumulatively impact project viability and housing affordability.
To address this, Rehda proposed for a review of government-imposed costs and regulatory requirements affecting residential development, including infrastructure, utility, statutory, regulatory, and compliance-related charges.
The association also called for the government to avoid introducing new or increased charges without considering their cumulative impact on housing affordability.
Rehda also called for affordability impact assessments for major new policies, regulations, standards and charges affecting residential development.
Meanwhile, the association noted that high initial investment required for modern construction technologies remains a barrier to adoption, particularly for small and medium-sized developers.
There are significant upfront costs associated with Building Information Modelling (BIM), Industrialised Building System (IBS), artificial intelligence (AI), automation, software, equipment, system integration, and training.
To encourage the adoption of the modern construction technology, Rehda proposes for targeted fiscal incentives, inclusing provision of accelerated capital allowance or investment tax allowance for qualifying BIM, IBS, AI, automation, software, and equipment expenditure.
It also called for enhanced or double tax deductions for qualifying implementation, integration, cybersecurity, training, and professional certification costs.
While sustainable housing and green building practices are becoming the norm, Rehda noted that existing green incentives do not adequately benefit all property segments, especially residential developments built for sale.
It also noted that the current green investment tax allowances (GITA) claim process is relatively restrictive, and higher green standards often entail additional upfront costs for both developers and purchasers.
To address this, Rehda proposed for the broadening of fiscal incentives for green property development by extending the existing GITA and green income tax exemption schemes for a further 10 years to provide long-term policy certainty and encourage sustained investment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dollar at 2-month highs as Fed outlook 'dominant'
Article:
LONDON: The dollar rose to its strongest level in two months on Wednesday on prospects of interest rate hikes in the near term, although easing oil prices could alter the global inflation and monetary policy outlook.
The euro fell to its lowest since late July and was last down 0.25 per cent at US$1.142. Sterling was down 0.3 per cent at US$1.3305. The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six others, was 0.24 per cent higher at 100.79.
The recent barrage of rate hikes and hawkish rhetoric from major central banks has taken centre stage in currency markets as the US-Israeli conflict with Iran drives oil prices higher and fans inflation worries.
Investors are now anticipating further rate rises and a number of Federal Reserve officials have this week signalled more policy tightening may be forthcoming if inflation does not subside quickly enough.
"It's another sign that the Fed story is dominant, and the hawkish Fedspeak is enough to keep USD in demand," ING strategist Francesco Pesole said.
Oil markets remain in the spotlight. Brent crude futures edged back above US$99 a barrel, breaking a five-day stretch of declines that was built on hopes that diplomacy at the UN General Assembly could pave the way for a resolution to the seven-month-long Middle East war.
Brent futures have risen 37 per cent since the conflict erupted at the end of February, while physical prices are at least 75 per cent higher in Europe and at least 40 per cent higher in the US.
"Whether this evolves into a more sustained decline remains to be seen. From a rates perspective, oil floating around the US$90-100/bbl range is unlikely to force a dovish rethink in market expectations," Pesole said.
Crude may be off its recent peaks, but refined product prices are still sky-high. The cost of diesel, which powers most transport, has shot to record highs in the US and to multi-year highs in Europe.
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he backed the idea of a diesel export ban as a way to lower domestic prices - something analysts say could do more harm than good to global supply flows.
In his speech at the UN on Tuesday, Trump warned that he could annihilate Iran if there is no deal to end the war, but also suggested an agreement could come soon as diplomatic efforts continued in New York.
"The good news is that oil prices have moderated somewhat from the highs but the path forward remains unclear given the lack of clarity around a possible resolution of the conflict," said Michael Wan, a currency analyst at MUFG.
Investors are also waiting for a high-stakes meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping as the two leaders seek stability in a relationship under pressure over wide-ranging issues.
The Japanese yen was at 157.8 per dollar as traders remain wary of the threat of intervention after the Bank of Japan's rate hike to a 31-year high last week fell short of reassuring investors that more increases may be on the way.
Japanese markets are closed for a holiday and this period of lower liquidity is seen by analysts as an optimal time for authorities to intervene, if needed.
"160 (per US dollar) remains the risk, but officials have reportedly moved away from telegraphing intervention and from any fixed level, so the cap could come earlier and in other forms," Intouch's Williams said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wife questions husband's late-night outings, gets slapped, headbutted and choked
Article:
KANGAR: A housewife who confronted her husband over his frequent late-night outings was slapped, headbutted and choked, at a house in Kampung Permatang Pauh, Simpang Empat, here.
Kangar police chief Assistant Commissioner Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the incident, which occurred around 9.30pm was believed to have stemmed from a misunderstanding between the 49-year-old victim and her 56-year-old husband, who works as a lorry driver.
He said the woman had earlier confronted her husband and asked him not to leave the house at night as she suspected he wanted to meet another woman.
"The suspect became angry after his wife accused him of having another woman and slapped the left side of her face before headbutting her on the forehead.
"The victim, who tried to defend herself, scratched the suspect's shoulder. However, the suspect pushed her, causing her to fall onto a sofa in the living room, before attempting to choke her," he said in a statement today.
Yusharifuddin said the altercation was brought under control by the victim's daughter, who was in the kitchen and heard the commotion in the living room, before the victim fled into the bedroom.
"Further investigations found that the woman had been abused by her husband for almost two years and claimed that she had previously been beaten unconscious.
"Following the latest incident, the victim suffered bruising to her abdomen and was advised to seek treatment and further examination at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital (HTF), Kangar.
"Police arrested the suspect to assist investigations and he has been remanded for four days until Sept 26.
"The case is being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code and Section 18 of the Domestic Violence Act," he said.

Title: Rising costs, end-financing pose as challenges to property development in 1H 2026 – Rehda survey
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian property developers continue to face considerable pressure from rising costs, financing constraints, and uncertainties in the wider economic environment, according to Rehda Malaysia president Datuk Zaini Yusoff.
While launch and sales numbers continue to hold up in the first half of the year, Zaini noted that the continuing challenges surrounding end-financing and affordability remain a particular concern among property developers, as costs continue to rise.
"Housing affordability should not be viewed solely from the perspective of property prices. Apart from access to appropriate end-financing, the cost of producing and delivering housing must also form part of the affordability equation," said Zaini in a statement released by Rehda today.
Cost pressures were widespread during the first half of 2026, with 81 per cent of survey respondents reporting an increase in the cost of doing business.
Of those respondents, 35 per cent experienced cost increases of between three and six per cent.
These findings were outlined in the Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association (Rehda) Property Industry Survey for the first half of 2026 and Market Outlook for the second half of 2026 and first half of 2027, which gathered responses from 181 Rehda members across Peninsular Malaysia to assess industry performance.
According to the survey, developers reported an average 13 per cent increase in construction costs between March and June 2026, which was attributed to rising fuel prices and ongoing geopolitical uncertainties.
During 1H 2026, 63 per cent of respondents encountered construction-related challenges, specifically involving building materials and labor.
The wider economic environment directly impacted operations, with 62 per cent of respondents indicating that economic conditions had affected their businesses.
In response to these pressures, developers implemented cost-cutting measures, including freezing recruitment, reducing employee benefits, and retrenchment, with 63 per cent of respondents expecting their companies to freeze hiring between July 2026 and June 2027, Rehda found.
Companies also rescheduled planned launches, delayed projects due to poor demand, and reduced the scale of their launches, said Rehda.
Financing constraints remain a primary hurdle, contributing to a high number of unsold properties.
As of June 30, 59 per cent of respondents reported having unsold completed residential units, the survey found.
The three main reasons cited for these unsold units were end-financing loan rejection, high property prices, and unreleased Bumiputera units.
The main factors contributing to housing loan rejections included purchasers' income eligibility, lower margins of financing offered by financial institutions, and applicants' adverse credit histories.
Despite these pressures, Zaini observed a consistency in launch numbers and a modest improvement in sales, suggesting that market demand is still present.
During 1H 2026, 54 respondents launched 15,834 units, remaining broadly unchanged from the 15,841 units recorded in 2H 2025.
Sales performance saw a 3.2 per cent increase, moving from 5,098 units in 2H 2025 to 5,260 units in 1H 2026. This brought the overall take-up rate up to 33.2 per cent, compared to 32.2 per cent in the preceding six months.
The majority of these sales were apartments and condominiums at 3,032 units, followed by serviced residences (1,114 units) and double and triple-storey terraces (610 units).
Of the newly launched units, 53 per cent were priced between RM300,001 and RM500,000, and were mostly located in Perak, Pahang, and Negri Sembilan.
Zaini said continued collaboration among the government, financial institutions and the industry is important to ensure that Malaysians who are financially capable of owning a home are able to do so.
"It is equally important for the relevant authorities to review statutory, regulatory and other compliance-related costs, particularly those which may no longer necessary or relevant, as these ultimately add to the cost of housing delivery," he said.
Looking ahead to 2H 2026, developers remain selective, with only 37 per cent of respondents indicating plans to launch. These planned launches involve 18,696 units, the majority of which will be strata units.
The 63 per cent of respondents without new launch plans cited unfavourable market conditions, delays in approval, and a higher number of unsold stocks as their top three reasons.
However, 56 per cent of respondents indicated plans to expand their land banks between July 2026 and June 2027, showing continued investment in long-term development opportunities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit ends higher against major currencies, weakens versus US dollar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended higher against major currencies on Wednesday but weakened against the greenback as expectations of further interest rate hikes by the United States Federal Reserve (Fed) continued to support the US dollar.
At 6pm, the ringgit edged down to 4.0780/0825 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0730/0775.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said markets expect the Fed to raise interest rates by another 50 basis points this year, providing further support to the US dollar.
"The ringgit actually started the day stronger, reaching RM4.0640 against the US dollar in the morning. But it could not maintain that strength. As the US dollar remained firm, the ringgit weakened to around RM4.0780 in the afternoon.
"Other Asian currencies also showed mixed movements, so the ringgit's performance was not completely isolated," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit traded higher against a basket of major currencies.
It gained against the euro to 4.6522/6573 from 4.6705/6757 at Tuesday's close and advanced vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.4156/4216 from 5.4452/4512. It also strengthened against the Japanese yen to 2.5836/5868 from 2.5958/5988 previously.
The local note traded mixed against its Asean peers.
It appreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.1909/1947 from 3.1955/1993 at Tuesday's close and strengthened versus the Thai baht to 12.2599/2782 from 12.2847/3035.
However, the ringgit declined against the Indonesian rupiah to 228.8/229.2 from 227.7/228.0 and weakened against the Philippine peso to 6.51/6.52 from 6.49/6.50.

Title: 'I follow Chief Secretary's directive, continue duties in Negri Sembilan as usual,' says Zafir
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim said he would continue performing his duties as usual, in accordance with the directive issued by the Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
He said the Chief Secretary had instructed him to remain in his post and continue serving in Negri Sembilan.
"Tan Sri asked me to continue performing my duties as usual. As a federal civil servant posted to Negri Sembilan, I will comply with the directive.
"However, I have an official engagement elsewhere today," he said.
This followed Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk
Ismail Lasim
's recent announcement that the state government had suspended Zafir and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal with immediate effect.
However, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said Zafir and Muzalmah must
continue performing their duties
as usual, as Ismail's decision to suspend them was invalid.
Yesterday, the Attorney-General's Chambers said matters relating to their appointments, as well as the suspension of the two office-holders, fall under the jurisdiction of the
Public Service Commission
and the Judicial and Legal Service Commission.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke maintains decision to quit Cabinet
Article:
HANGZHOU: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he is sticking to his decision to quit the Cabinet.
Loke, who is Transport Minister, said he will submit his resignation letter once he returns to Malaysia from China.
"The decision has been made. I will submit it (my resignation letter) to the prime minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) once I return to Malaysia," he said briefly when met by reporters upon arrival in Hangzhou.
Loke, who is the Seremban member of parliament, was responding to a question on whether he would go through with his earlier decision to withdraw from the Cabinet.
He is currently among the federal ministers accompanying the prime minister on a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, at the invitation of the Chinese government.
Loke had previously announced that he would tender his resignation as the transport minister following the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
He made the
announcement
after the DAP's Central Executive Committee meeting on Sept 19.
However, he said other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain within the federal administration.
Earlier today, Anwar said he had advised Loke to
reconsider
his earlier intention to resign.
Anwar said DAP should not bow to pressure from parties with political interests to withdraw from the government simply because they wanted to see the unity government become unstable.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget : Construction, AI, infrastructure sectors to benefit – Moomoo
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: 2027 Budget, to be tabled on Oct 9, is expected to benefit the construction and building materials sectors, based on current market consensus of RM85 billion to RM90 billion in development expenditure, according to Moomoo.
The online trading and investment platform said the sectors could benefit particularly from contracts involving hospitals, schools and transport infrastructure.
It said beyond traditional construction materials, grid and water infrastructure, renewable energy and energy storage could also benefit from development spending.
"Semiconductors and artificial intelligence-linked names will continue to ride the data centre and National AI Action Plan wave.
"Lastly, targeted cash aids like BUDI95 would support value and affordable consumer stocks by protecting baseline household purchasing power," it said in a statement.
But steel and high-carbon energy producers could face pressure from the proposed carbon tax, which would introduce additional compliance costs.
Moomoo said discretionary consumer stocks may face headwinds from the potential expansion or adjustment of the Sales and Service Tax (SST) framework, as middle-class spending power may come under pressure.
It added that tobacco and alcohol stocks could face pre-Budget uncertainty over potential excise duty increases.
For investors, Moomoo said diversification across sectors will be important, with opportunities spanning Bursa-listed companies and global companies linked to the AI and semiconductor cycle.
Moomoo noted that current market consensus estimates put 2027 Budget's total expenditure at around RM438.9 billion, comprising approximately RM353.1 billion in operating expenditure and RM85.8 billion in development expenditure.
This is broadly in line with the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) 2026-2030, which provides for average development expenditure of RM86 billion annually.
Beyond the headline spending figure, Moomoo said two key policy areas that could influence market sentiment and foreign capital flows are fuel subsidies and fiscal discipline, and taxation and government revenue.
On subsidies, the government's ability to balance rising global energy costs with fiscal discipline will be closely watched, particularly after the BUDI95 basic subsidy quota was restored to 300 litres per month at RM1.99 per litre from Sept 1, benefiting more than 16 million people.
With the 2026 fuel subsidy bill potentially reaching RM40 billion, Moomoo said the government's ability to maintain fiscal discipline while protecting households will remain under scrutiny.
On taxation, the market does not expect major new taxes; the focus is likely to remain on optimising the existing tax framework, including SST and the capital gains tax on unlisted shares.
The increase in the mandatory e-Invoicing threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million in annual revenue from Sept 1 also provides relief for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), while the proposed carbon tax targeting the steel and energy sectors remains an area to watch.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 13 areas in Sarawak record unhealthy API readings, Serian highest at 197
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Thirteen areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today, with the Serian district police headquarters recording the highest reading at 197.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas with unhealthy API readings were Kuching (184), Samarahan (181), Sri Aman (176), Bintulu (174), Sibu (167) and Sarikei (165).
Unhealthy readings were also recorded in Samalaju (164), Miri (161), Mukah (160), Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (155), Limbang (153) and Kapit (120).
Meanwhile, 45 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while nine recorded good readings.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No motion of no confidence submitted yet – Johari
Article:
BANGI: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul has yet to receive any motion of no confidence for the upcoming parliamentary sitting.
"Not even one (motion of no confidence) has been received. I have not heard anything about it," he told reporters after officiating the 'Negara Bangsa: Membina Jati Diri dan Identiti Nasional' dialogue here today.
His remarks came after Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi challenged any party seeking to remove Umno and Barisan Nasional from the Unity Government to formally do so by tabling a no-confidence motion in the Dewan Rakyat.
Johari also said he had yet to receive the proposed Bills on the separation of the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor, as well as the Bill to limit the prime minister's tenure.
"I was informed that there were plans for them, but I have yet to receive the papers. Usually, two weeks before the tabling, the Speaker will be informed. But so far, I have not received anything," he said.
Earlier, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bill to limit the prime minister's tenure was ready to be tabled in the upcoming parliamentary session.
According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar on the Parliament website, the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament will run for 37 days from Oct 5 to Dec 8, with Budget 2027 scheduled to be tabled on Oct 9.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Technician gets RM20,000 bail over restaurant assault
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A technician charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt to a businessman during an assault at a restaurant has been granted RM20,000 bail with one surety.
High Court judge Nurulhuda Nur'aini Mohamad Nor allowed the bail application by Lai Kae Bin, 33.
The court ordered Lai to surrender his passport until the disposal of the case, report weekly to the Kepong police station and refrain from approaching the victim and witnesses.
Earlier, lawyer Muhamad Firdaus Jumaludin applied for bail, saying his client was not a flight risk and needed to care for his ailing mother following his father's death.
Firdaus said a review of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed that Lai's involvement in the incident was minor.
"Some of the footage showed that Lai was not the person who initiated the attack and had attempted to stop it.
"Moreover, the presumption of innocence applies," he said, adding that the prosecution's proposed bail of RM30,000 was excessive.
Deputy public prosecutor Haslida Ismail objected to the bail application, urging the court to consider the severity of the offence, the risk of witness interference and the possibility of the accused absconding.
She also questioned whether the proposed surety, who was not Lai's immediate relative, was sufficient to ensure his compliance with the bail conditions and attendance in court.
"The victim was traumatised by the incident. The prosecution is concerned that the accused might approach or interfere with the victim if released," she said.
Nurulhuda also reminded the surety of his responsibility to ensure that Lai attends court, failing which the bail sum would be forfeited.
Firdaus had previously said Lai had instructed him to seek a lesser charge, as he believed the existing charge under Section 326 of the Penal Code was too serious.
Lai's representation to the Attorney-General's Chambers is still under review.
Lai is one of three men charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt to businessman Andrew Teh, 47, using dangerous weapons at Restoran Hing Kee Bakuteh in Jalan Kepong at 2am on May 7.
The other two accused are carpenter Wong Weng Luen, 49, and memorial centre worker Wan Ken Fei, 30.
All 3 have pleaded not guilty to the charge.
Wong is currently undergoing psychiatric assessment at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak following a court order issued last month.
Wan had previously applied for bail but was denied.
The attack allegedly stemmed from an incident in which Teh was accused of staring at a man believed to be intoxicated while dining at the restaurant.
CCTV footage of the several-minute assault later went viral on social media.
The footage showed Teh seated at a table before one of the men approached and began attacking him.
Two others then joined in, initially appearing to restrain their friend before taking part in the assault.
Teh was punched, kicked and struck with various objects, including chairs and a kettle, before managing to escape.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UUCA replacement Bill expected to be tabled in December, says Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The first reading of the Bill to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU) is expected to be tabled at the Dewan Rakyat sitting in December, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
He said the ministry is working to complete a comprehensive series of engagements with stakeholders to ensure the Bill accounts for the entire national higher education ecosystem before it is tabled in Parliament.
“In terms of timeline, we will try to see whether we can carry out the first reading, perhaps at the December parliamentary sitting.
“But you must remember, it (the Bill) will involve very extensive engagement,” he said after the closing ceremony of the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit (URIIS) 2026 here today.
He added that the draft Bill is not confined to student freedom, but also covers administrative structure, university governance and academic aspects.
He explained that AUKU contains 44 sections, of which seven involve students, while the rest cover matters related to the establishment of universities, university governance, academics and others.
“We understand that when drafting a new act, we must take into account the entire ecosystem of the national higher education system,” he said.
Zambry said the latest series of engagements was held with the Parliamentary Special Select Committee to obtain feedback from both government and opposition representatives.
Meanwhile, turning to Budget 2027, Zambry expressed hope that the Higher Education Ministry would secure a larger allocation to support the Malaysian Higher Education Development Plan. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: AUKU is the acronym derived from the Malay name of the Act.

Title: ADB raises Malaysia’s 2026, 2027 growth forecasts to 4.9pc, 4.7pc
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has raised its 2026 and 2027 economic growth forecasts for Malaysia to 4.9 per cent and 4.7 per cent, respectively.
This is supported by the semiconductor upcycle, while data centre investments reinforce consumption and construction. The latest forecasts are higher than the 4.6 per cent forecast for 2026 and 4.5 per cent for 2027 in the Asian Development Outlook (ADO) July 2026 report.
In its September 2026 report, ADB said Malaysia’s growth is expected to moderate slightly in the second half of 2026 (2H 2026) and in 2027.
“The West Asia conflict disrupted supply chains and elevated international prices, which can impact domestic costs, thus constraining household consumption and business activity.  The uncertain external environment will continue to weigh on growth. Growth in 2027 will likely slow further from El Nino‑related disruptions to local output and continued pressures on food and energy costs,” it said.
Malaysia’s inflation will likely remain at 2.0 per cent through the rest of 2026 and for 2027, according to ADO.
Domestic spending will likely remain resilient, but heightened downside pressures may limit labour and consumption growth, it said. Labour market prospects should be bolstered by tourism in 2H 2026, alongside Visit Malaysia 2026 initiatives and the upcoming Formula One event in Sepang.
“Continuing fuel subsidies and cash transfers to low-income households will support household spending. However, persistently high prices could limit household spending and restrain consumption growth,” it added.
In addition, construction and investment should remain robust, supported by a second data center boom expected in 2H 2026 as hyperscalers begin megacampus developments in Springhill, Serendah, and Johor.
The sector will be further supported by major public infrastructure projects such as the Penang light rail transit and Kerian water project in Perak rollout in the coming months.
The report said manufacturing and external trade will likely be bolstered by further developments and use of artificial intelligence (AI), and growth will likely remain strong, with global semiconductor sales projected to climb to US$1.5 trillion (RM6.1 trillion) in 2026, up from US$795.6 billion in 2025. — Bernama

Title: SPR: Postal voting applications for Melaka polls open today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 —Applications for all categories of domestic and overseas postal voting for the 16th Melaka State Election open today.
Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said all applications must be submitted online via the MySPR portal at
https://myspr.spr.gov.my
, with the closing date to be announced later.
“Eligible voters who intend to cast their ballots by post must register for or have an existing MySPR account before submitting their application,” he said in a statement today.
Khairul Shahril said applications under Category 1A cover police and military personnel, election officials, EC members and staff, as well as media personnel.
Applications are also open for Category 1B, for Malaysians residing abroad, and Category 1C, for agencies or organisations.
Those with further enquiries can contact the hotline at 03-88927080 or email
upup@spr.gov.my
.
Yesterday, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly, effective today, to pave the way for the 16th state election, following the consent of Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
Melaka State Assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum also submitted the dissolution notice to the EC yesterday.
In the 15th Melaka State Election on Nov 20, 2021, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 state seats to form the state government with a more than two-thirds majority, while Pakatan Harapan secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional two. — Bernama

Title: ‘Decision has been made’: Anthony Loke firm on resignation, to hand in letter upon return from China
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he remains firm in his decision to resign as Transport Minister.
The Seremban MP said he would hand in his resignation letter upon returning home from China.
“The decision has been made. I will submit the resignation letter to the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) when I return home,” he told reporters briefly after arriving in Hangzhou today.
He is currently accompanying the Prime Minister on a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou at the invitation of the Chinese government.
Loke offered to resign following a DAP Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting on Saturday in response to the conditional pardon granted to former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak.
He said the other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the Unity Government.
Speaking to Malaysian media while travelling from Shanghai to Hangzhou by high-speed train, Anwar said he would not rush into a decision on Loke’s intention to resign as Transport Minister, adding that he wanted to hear Loke’s explanation first.
The Prime Minister added that DAP should not bow to calls from parties he described as having political interests for it to withdraw from the government. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan candidates to be announced one to two weeks ahead of nomination, says PM’s pol-sec
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Sept 23 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election one to two weeks before nomination day, said Prime Minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin.
He said the move would allow PH to make early preparations instead of waiting until the last minute to finalise its candidates.
“This time, we are better prepared to name our candidates,” he told reporters after visiting beneficiaries under the Ziarah Kasih programme at the Kuala Linggi state constituency here today.
Azman said the candidate selection process would be left to the party leadership, taking into account lists submitted by party divisions, state leaders and the grassroots before the final decision is made.
Earlier, Azman visited seven recipients under the Ziarah Kasih programme, including a single mother with two children who is unable to work after being involved in a road accident.
The programme also provided cash assistance from the Prime Minister’s Department, as well as follow-up aid such as wheelchairs or other support where required and eligible.
Azman said the Ziarah Kasih programme was among the activities carried out by the Political Secretary’s Office and would continue in several other areas in Melaka, including the Jasin parliamentary constituency next week. — Bernama

Title: Police announce three‑stage road closures for Kuching Marathon from Sept 26 to 27
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 23 — Road closures and traffic diversions for the Kuching Marathon 2026 will be implemented in three stages from midday Saturday (September 26) until Sunday morning (September 27).
Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the first closures would begin at noon on September 26 and involve Lebuh Wayang-Jalan Main Bazaar, Jalan Main Bazaar-Jalan Tun Abang Haji Openg, and Jalan Tun Abang Haji Openg-Carpenter Street.
These three locations will remain closed until 10am on September 27 to facilitate preparations for the event.
The Jalan Barrack-Jalan Pearl junction will then be closed from 10pm on September 26 until 10am the following day.
From 12.01am to 10am on September 27, closures and diversions will be implemented at another 22 locations along the marathon route.
These include the Jalan Pearl-Jalan Wawasan traffic lights towards Padang Merdeka, Lebuh Wayang-Jalan Wawasan, Jalan McDougall-Jalan Tun Abang Haji Openg, and Susur Jalan Haji Taha.
Also affected are the Jalan Ajibah Abol traffic lights, Jalan Muhibbah-Jalan Kulas junction, Jalan Tun Abdul Rahman Yaakob-Jalan Merdeka junction, Jalan Kampung Lintang-Jalan Astana traffic lights, Mahkamah roundabout, Sesco roundabout, and Samariang roundabout.
The closures will also cover the Jalan Sultan Tengah traffic lights near the fire station and Sego, Yayasan roundabout, Kesuma Resort roundabout, Stadium roundabout, Gersik roundabout, Merrican Salleh-Jalan Kwong Lee Bank traffic lights, Tanah Putih Clinic traffic lights, Jalan Sekama-Pending traffic lights, Sri Aman roundabout, and Jalan Gamelan-Jalan Tun Abdul Rahman Yaakob junction.
“PDRM seeks the cooperation of the public not to park vehicles along road shoulders and advises motorists to plan their journeys and use alternative routes to reduce traffic congestion,” Alexson said in a statement.
For more information, contact the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at the Kuching District Police Headquarters on 082-259900. — The Borneo Post
Map shows the route for the 42km full marathon. — Picture via Facebook/Kuching Marathon

Title: Man dies in suspected electrocution in Lahad Datu
Article:
LAHAD DATU, Sept 23 — A man in his 30s died after he was believed to have been electrocuted at Kampung Puyut here today.
The man, who had yet to be identified, was believed to have no identification document and was not recognised by local villagers, said Lahad Datu Fire and Rescue Station chief Sumsoa Rashid.
He said the department received a distress call at 12.47pm and deployed 12 personnel to the scene, where the man was found electrocuted and was later confirmed dead by Health Ministry personnel.
The victim was retrieved using a stretcher and rope after Sabah Electricity cut off the electricity supply in the area, before his body was handed over to police, with the operation ending at 1.36pm.
Earlier, a man in his 40s suffered burns when a 30x40-foot house at Jalan Hilir was 90 per cent destroyed by fire at 10.32am, with the victim taken to hospital by members of the public and the fire brought under control at 12.09pm. — Daily Express

Title: Bring umbrellas: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected in KL and 10 states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur and 10 states until 6pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the states affected are Kedah, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Johor, Sarawak and Sabah.
In Kedah, the areas expected to be affected are Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, the warning covers Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang, Kerian, Kuala Kangsar, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak.
The same warning has been issued for Kelantan, covering Jeli and Kuala Krai; Terengganu (Kemaman, Dungun, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Setiu and Hulu Terengganu); and Pahang (Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut, Lipis and Kuantan).
Bad weather is also expected to hit Selangor (Petaling, Gombak and Hulu Langat); Negeri Sembilan (Jelebu and Jempol); and Johor (Kulai, Kluang, Kota Tinggi, Mersing, Johor Bahru, Batu Pahat, Muar, Tangkak and Segamat).
In Sabah, the warning covers Sandakan (Kinabatangan), Tawau (Lahad Datu, Tawau and Kalabakan), Interior (Pensiangan, Tambunan, Tenom, Membakut, Beaufort, Kuala Penyu, Keningau and Sipitang) and West Coast.
In Sarawak, the areas expected to be affected are Limbang and Miri (Bario, Marudi, Miri and Telang Usan). — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Negeri Sembilan MB and executive council’s bid to remove ruler was ‘rude and uncivilised’
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim criticised the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar and state executive council for attempting to remove Yang di‑Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, calling the move rude and uncivilised.
He said no state‑level authority has the mandate to question or alter the position of the Ruler, according to
Berita Harian
.
“Menteri Besar and the executive council who made this decision — this is a rude step, uncivilised, and I strongly object,” he said while travelling by high‑speed train from Shanghai to Hangzhou.
Anwar said the crisis involving state administration and customary authority in Negeri Sembilan had become increasingly complex.
He noted that Datuk Ismail Lasim previously announced that the proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz had been unanimously endorsed by the state executive council.
Anwar stressed that the federal government is not interfering in the matter and said the issue of dethroning a Ruler is not straightforward.
He said his recent audience with Tuanku Muhriz was held because the court had affirmed His Majesty as the lawful Yang di‑Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
He said the Undang Luak have the authority to decide on the position of the Ruler, but their decisions are not absolute and must follow established procedures.
“I respect the Undang, and I know some of them well, but they must understand that safeguarding national institutions and security is the responsibility of the federal government,” he said.
“Do not say we cannot be involved; this is not interference. The Undang can make decisions, but those decisions are not absolute and must follow the rules,” he added.
Anwar said conflicting claims among the Undang must be resolved before any decision can be considered valid.
He said any decision made by the properly appointed Undang following the correct process would fall outside the jurisdiction of the federal government.

Title: Anwar asks Loke to review decision to quit Cabinet after Najib’s conditional pardon
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged Transport Minister Anthony Loke to rethink his plan to step down from the Cabinet following the Pardons Board’s decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon.
In a
New Straits Times
report, Anwar said DAP should not give in to political pressure from groups seeking instability in the unity government.
“Some people ask, why Anthony Loke? Why doesn’t the whole of DAP leave? Whose suggestion is that? Why should he leave? He did nothing wrong,” he said while travelling by high‑speed train from Shanghai to Hangzhou.
He said Loke had not proposed the pardon and had “tried his best to oppose it.”
“So I think DAP should not bow to pressure from those with vested interests because they want the government to be unstable,” he added.
Anwar said he would meet Loke soon to hear his explanation and would ask him to withdraw his decision to resign.
He acknowledged that DAP and Pakatan Harapan had long taken a firm stance against kleptocracy and corruption, making the Pardons Board’s decision difficult for them to defend.
“I gave him space and did not want to rush things because I respect his decision. He is not opposing my decision or the Madani government or cooperation within the unity government,” he said.
“He feels it is difficult to defend the Pardons Board’s decision when his party, and even Pakatan Harapan, has held a very firm position on this matter from the beginning.”
Anwar said the government’s views, including the position taken by Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar during the Pardons Board meeting, had been conveyed to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
He reminded all parties that executive power has constitutional limits and that the final decision on pardons rests with the King.
Anwar criticised politicians who alleged there was a compromise or secret pact between him and Umno leaders over the pardon.
He said his administration’s priority was to maintain political stability, uphold good relations with the Malay Rulers and steer the country’s economic direction responsibly.
He also urged Malaysians of all backgrounds to uphold loyalty to the nation through the term “Wangyue,” which he said symbolises commitment to the country.

Title: Structural checks at Cheras apartment will take several days following landslide, says Selangor exco
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Residents evacuated from Block D of the Damai Perdana Apartments in Cheras may have to remain out of their homes for several days while authorities determine whether the building is structurally safe.
Kajang Municipal Council (MPKj) Zone 6 councillor Tan Kah Hoe said multiple technical agencies were conducting assessments of the affected block, according to
New Straits Times
.
“It depends on the reports from the technical agencies I mentioned earlier, namely the Public Works Department, Drainage and Irrigation Department and Minerals and Geoscience Department, because at this point, we still do not know whether the building’s structure is safe for occupation,” he said today.
Tan said he had asked the agencies to complete their evaluations as quickly as possible.
He said the agencies informed him that the reports would take several days to finalise.
Residents of an apartment block in Bandar Damai Perdana, Cheras were ordered to evacuate their homes last night after a landslide occurred near the building, believed to have been caused by an underground water leak. — Bernama pic
Authorities ordered the evacuation of about 80 residents from 45 units after a slope failure occurred near Block D around 8pm yesterday.
The evacuation was carried out as a precaution while officials examined the stability of the slope and the condition of the building.
Residents living near the slope at the Bandar Damai Perdana apartment complex were instructed to leave their homes after the landslide occurred close to the block.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 9.03pm regarding the incident.
He said an underground water leak was believed to have caused the landslide.
Ashrul said the affected slope measured about 4.57m in height, and the slipped earth was approximately 0.91m from the impacted area.
