Title: Sabah man bites ex-girlfriend and threatens to kill her, gets RM5,800 fine
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 23 — A 35-year-old man was fined RM5,800 after pleading guilty to hurting his ex-girlfriend and threatening to kill her.
Mohd Aideed Husein pleaded guilty before two Magistrates, Dzul Elmy Yunus and Marilyn Kelvin, to separate charges over the incident involving the 30-year-old woman on Sept 15.
Before Dzul Elmy, he was fined RM1,800, in default six months’ jail, under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt to the woman outside a shop at Lorong Suria Inanam 1.
Before Marilyn, he was fined RM4,000, in default nine months’ jail, under Section 506 of the Penal Code for threatening to kill the victim at the same place and on the same day.
The court heard that the couple had quarrelled inside a car before Mohd Aideed threatened to kill her if she ended their relationship, and subsequently hit and bit her right arm.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Akaash Singh prosecuted while Mohd Aideed was unrepresented. — Daily Express

Title: Expedite court proceedings to settle Negeri Sembilan royal dispute, says ex-minister Syed Hamid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Court proceedings related to the Negeri Sembilan royal institution dispute should be expedited to provide a definitive resolution to the legal questions involved, former law minister Tan Sri Syed Hamid Albar said.
He said the dispute, which involves the
adat
(customary practices), state law and the Federal Constitution, should be resolved through the legal process rather than public debate or sentiment.
“When one party says it has a right and another party says the same, there is clearly a dispute that needs to be determined.
“The courts should expedite whatever hearings are necessary to resolve these legal questions,” he told Bernama when contacted today.
Syed Hamid, who has also served as home and foreign minister, said those with jurisdiction over the matter, including the Attorney-General and the government, were entitled to carry out their respective responsibilities, and their should not be regarded as interference unless a court determines otherwise.
Syed Hamid also urged all parties to refrain from making conflicting public statements, saying these could heighten public anxiety and make it more difficult to reach a reasonable and rational resolution.
“Malaysians are confused, and outsiders are also confused. This is no longer an internal matter involving a particular group or state because it has become a public dispute that people want to see resolved.
“This affects confidence. It is not good for Malaysian politics or public perception,” he said.
Syed Hamid said any action involving a person’s position or removal from office must be carried out in accordance with the procedures and provisions set out in the Constitution and relevant laws. — Bernama

Title: AG says Negeri Sembilan state secretary and legal adviser remain in office, must continue duties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said Negeri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal must continue carrying out their duties because their suspension by Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim is invalid.
He said both officers cannot be barred from entering their offices, as preventing them from working would be unlawful, according to the
New Straits Times.
Dusuki said, “The duties of Mohd Zafir as Negeri Sembilan state secretary and Muzalmah as state legal adviser must continue as usual, and they must also remain in Negeri Sembilan.”
He added that the menteri besar’s order to suspend them “is invalid and can simply be disregarded.”
The Attorney General’s Chambers said last night that the Negeri Sembilan state executive council has no legal authority to suspend either officer, as appointments and suspensions fall under the Public Service Commission and the Judicial and Legal Service Commission.
The chambers also said any new appointment of a state legal adviser must comply with Article 37 of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 and be made by the Judicial and Legal Service Commission from among its members.
Ismail had earlier said the state executive council unanimously decided at a special meeting to suspend Mohd Zafir and Muzalmah with immediate effect.
Dusuki said the situation in Negeri Sembilan mirrors the 2009 Perak crisis, when the state secretary and state legal adviser were also suspended.
He said that in 2009, then Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Sidek Hassan and the Attorney General’s Chambers decided that the Perak menteri besar did not have the power to suspend the two senior officers.
He said the Perak state secretary and legal adviser were subsequently instructed to continue performing their duties as usual.

Title: Kota Bharu trader’s no-show lands him an arrest warrant over 42 cooking oil charges
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 23 — The Sessions Court here today issued an arrest warrant for the owner of a subsidised cooking oil business after he failed to appear before the court to face charges involving the management of records and documents for the controlled item.
Judge Nik Habri Muhamad issued the arrest warrant for Pui Tiong Lam, 61, for failing to appear in court for today’s prosecution proceedings without a valid reason.
Pui was scheduled to be charged with 41 counts of failing to maintain stock records for subsidised cooking oil and one count of failing to produce documents relating to the controlled item today.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Siti Edabayu Subhan, from the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living, told the court that the prosecution had not received a medical certificate from Pui to explain his absence.
“Therefore, the prosecution applied for an arrest warrant to ensure that the accused can be brought before the court to face all the charges,” she said.
The court set Nov 5 for mention. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan telecoms at risk of major outages as cable vandalism and theft soar, says says regional MCMC official
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 23 — Vandalism and theft of telecommunications infrastructure in Kelantan have reached an alarming level and could disrupt communication coverage and the livelihoods of people if critical infrastructure is affected.
Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) Eastern Region Office senior director Mohd Fairus Muhamad said these incidents have also impacted the telecommunications industry, which bears millions of ringgit in losses for repair and restoration work.
“What is more concerning is that these estimates do not yet take into account the impact of disruptions on businesses and the daily activities of communities that depend on telecommunications services,” he said at the 2026 Kelantan state-level #TelecommunicationsInfrastructureVandalism Prevention Campaign here today.
He said disruptions to communication infrastructure not only affect technical systems but can also disrupt learning, work matters and business transactions, particularly for online entrepreneurs who depend on network stability.
He added that the impact of disruptions can be even greater if damage or theft occurs on infrastructure shared by multiple telecommunications service providers.
“If the infrastructure is shared by all telcos, any act of vandalism can cut off every line, and users, whether on CelcomDigi, Maxis, U Mobile or any other provider, can lose coverage,” he said.
Mohd Fairus said the recovery period also depends on the components stolen or damaged, especially if the equipment must be sourced from the telecommunications company’s headquarters outside Kelantan.
He said MCMC, together with enforcement authorities and industry players, is tightening coordination, including proposing a Telecommunications Infrastructure Vandalism Prevention Sub-Committee involving MCMC, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), local authorities, the Land and District Office and industry players.
Mohd Fairus said he has also asked PDRM to notify MCMC of related operations such as Ops Tembaga so that action can be coordinated, as vandalism cases involve multiple service providers, apart from Telekom Malaysia.
He urged the public to report suspicious activity involving telecommunications infrastructure to MCMC or the police, particularly in areas with high rates of vandalism and theft.
Mohd Fairus also reminded contractors and the public to use the Call Before You Dig initiative to prevent fibre optic cables from being severed by excavation work, which can cause large-scale service disruptions. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: PDRM is the abbreviation in Malay for Polis Diraja Malaysia.

Title: TVET graduates may have jobs, but are they the right jobs? MEF asks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has called for a broader assessment of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduate employability to better reflect their skills, career progression and contribution to the workforce.
MEF senior adviser for Government, Media and International Engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the federation supported Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir’s call for the employability of Polytechnic and Community College (PolyCC) graduates to be assessed beyond headline employment percentages.
He said the 2025 employability rates of 98.5 per cent for polytechnic graduates and 98.8 per cent for community college graduates were encouraging, but the quality and relevance of employment should also be considered in evaluating TVET outcomes.
“A graduate may be employed, but the critical question is whether the job utilises the skills acquired. We should distinguish between being employed and being appropriately employed,” he said in a statement today.
In this regard, Syed Hussain suggested that future TVET performance indicators should also take into account employment in fields relevant to graduates’ training, starting salaries and wage progression, career development, employer satisfaction and job readiness.
He said other indicators could include industry-recognised certifications, participation in lifelong learning, reskilling and upskilling, as well as graduates’ progression into higher-value and higher-skilled occupations.
He emphasised that technical competency remained fundamental, but graduates also needed strong communication, teamwork, problem-solving and adaptability skills to succeed in different workplace environments.
“We must remember that skills alone are not enough. Employers need people who can apply those skills in the real workplace, communicate effectively, work as part of a team, solve problems and adapt when circumstances change,” he said.
Syed Hussain said stronger collaboration between industry and educational institutions was essential to ensure TVET programmes remained aligned with changing workforce needs.
He proposed a stronger industry-to-classroom-to-workplace model, with employers involved in industry demand forecasting, curriculum design, practical training, competency assessment, certification, recruitment and continuous upskilling.
He said that such an approach would help ensure graduates were better prepared for the workplace while allowing TVET institutions to respond more quickly to technological and industry changes.
Syed Hussain also said that efforts to further strengthen TVET needed to be matched by the creation of more high-skilled employment opportunities for graduates.
He said producing skilled graduates without creating enough high-value jobs could lead to skills underemployment, while attracting high-value investments without developing the right talent could result in skills shortages.
Therefore, he said education, TVET, industrial and investment policies needed to move in the same direction to create sufficient opportunities for skilled graduates.
“If we want our TVET graduates to have good jobs, we must create more good jobs. Education policy and investment policy must move together.
“The Government must continue to bring in investments that are driven by technology, engineering, automation, digitalisation, advanced manufacturing, renewable energy, electric vehicles (EVs), aerospace, semiconductor-related activities, logistics, cybersecurity and other high-value sectors,” he said.
He said MEF remained committed to working with the Ministry of Higher Education, National TVET Council, PolyCC institutions and relevant agencies to strengthen industry-education collaboration and build a demand-driven, industry-led and future-ready TVET ecosystem. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 wishlist: Rehda wants wider housing loan access, special campaign for unsold units
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Enhancing the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) and introducing improved financing structures are among the proposals made by the Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) Malaysia for Budget 2027.
The association is also seeking an extension of existing stamp duty relief and a special Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) for unsold completed residential units.
Rehda president Datuk Zaini Yusoff said the proposals, which have been submitted to the Ministry of Housing and Local Government and the Ministry of Finance, are aimed at addressing constraints faced by homebuyers as well as the rising cost of housing delivery.
He said among the key proposals is an enhancement of the SJKP to widen access to financing, particularly for young Malaysians, the self-employed and those without fixed or conventional incomes.
“Access to housing financing remains a major barrier to house ownership, particularly for young Malaysians, the self-employed and purchasers with low or non-traditional incomes,” said Zaini at a media briefing on Rehda’s Property Industry Survey for the first half of 2026 (1H 2026) here today.
Rehda also proposed government-backed housing financing or guarantee mechanisms, as well as stepped-up financing structures that would allow lower repayments during the initial years of house ownership.
He said the measures would help prospective buyers who have the capacity to service monthly housing repayments but struggle with the upfront costs of purchasing a home.
Most prospective buyers, especially those in the Bottom 40 (B40) group, have the capacity to service their monthly housing repayments, but they face difficulty accumulating sufficient savings for stamp duty and other initial acquisition costs, said Zaini.
“Normally, coming up with that 10 per cent is difficult for them. So, we are asking the government to help on this,” he said.
On stamp duty, Zaini said Rehda proposed extending the existing relief to residential properties priced above RM500,000 and up to RM1 million, with an appropriate tiered relief mechanism for purchases made between January and December 2027.
He said Rehda has also proposed measures to address unsold completed residential units, including a special HOC for such properties that have obtained the Certificate of Completion and Compliance.
“There are a lot of overhang units, so we want to address these units first,” said Zaini.
Rehda’s survey indicates that 59 per cent of 181 respondents had unsold completed residential units as of June 30. The reasons cited include rejection of end-financing applications, high property prices, and unreleased Bumiputera units.
He said a targeted HOC could improve market liquidity and allow capital tied up in unsold properties to be recycled into new developments.
Rehda is advocating for data-driven housing planning to better align future housing supply with actual demand, preventing supply-demand mismatches.
Zaini emphasised that reducing the cost of housing delivery is another priority, given rising infrastructure, utility, statutory, regulatory and compliance costs borne by developers.
“Housing affordability is influenced not only by purchasers’ access to financing but also by the cost of developing and delivering homes.
“We are asking the government to look at these costs again. Once these are reduced, developers can also reduce prices significantly,” he said.
Rehda is also seeking fiscal incentives to accelerate construction productivity, technology adoption and digitalisation, including incentives for investments in Building Information Modelling, Industrialised Building System, artificial intelligence, automation, software and equipment.
Proposals include accelerated capital allowances and investment tax allowances for qualifying expenditures in these areas.
The association also called for measures to accelerate green and sustainable housing development as part of its Budget 2027 proposals. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: SJKP is the abbreviation in Malay for Skim Jaminan Kredit Perumahan.

Title: Who was he? A month on, mystery deepens over man found dead in KLIA aircraft landing gear
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 23 — The identity of a man whose body was found in an aircraft’s landing gear compartment at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 2 on Aug 27 remains unknown and the remains have yet to be claimed.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said police had yet to receive any information that could establish the man’s identity.
“So far, no one has come forward with any information. If there are family members whose relatives have not returned home or have gone missing, they can contact the nearest police station so that we can complete our investigation,” he told a press conference on the Selangor Criminal Investigation Department’s Narcotics Division achievements here today.
Asked how the man came to be inside the aircraft, Shazeli said the circumstances remained a mystery and were still under investigation.
“This is not the first such case. There have been instances where individuals were found in landing gear compartments. I do not want to draw any conclusions as this could lead us in the wrong direction. We will wait for the outcome of the investigation,” he said.
Meanwhile, Shazeli said police were tracing the owner and crew of a fishing boat who were alleged to have failed to retrieve the body of a victim in a boat tragedy, to have them give statements to assist the investigation.
He said police had recorded statements from the survivors as of yesterday, but several other individuals, particularly witnesses, had yet to have their statements recorded as their health had not permitted it.
“We are working to complete the investigation, including tracing the fishermen and owner of the boat allegedly used. Insya Allah, we will do our best to obtain the information needed and complete the investigation,” he said.
On the victim’s family questioning why the body was not retrieved when four survivors were found, Shazeli said police were still investigating the matter.
He said based on statements and information gathered from witnesses so far, the body could have belonged to a different individual and not one of the fishing group.
“Based on the statements and accounts of the witnesses involved, we believe the incident may have involved different individuals and not the same group. This is because identification could not be carried out at the time due to the condition of the body,” he said.
Four anglers survived the tragedy on Sept 13, namely Mohd Shairazi Abdul Aziz, 43; Mohd Rizal Mohamad Sadali, 45; Muhd Hamiszar Punirain, 45; and Zulfikalnain Awang, 47, while Mohamad Shahril Abd Rahman, 43, and Muhammad Ridzuan Ruhaizat, 37, were confirmed dead and Raja Mohd Rozi Raja Mohamud, 49, remains missing. — Bernama

Title: Former Kelantan Kafa teacher gets RM2,000 fine for kicking Year Five pupil in face during class
Article:
KUALA KRAI, Sept 23 — A former Religious and Fardu Ain Class (Kafa) teacher was fined RM2,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today for kicking a Year Five pupil in the face, causing injuries to his gums.
Magistrate Rais Imran Hamid imposed the maximum fine, with a default of four months in jail, after Abdullah Mustakim, 33, pleaded guilty to voluntarily causing hurt to the pupil in a classroom at a school here at about 2.30 pm on Oct 23, 2024.
Abdullah was charged under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum prison term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mazlinda Mohd Nor prosecuted, while Abdullah, who now works as a labourer earning RM1,000 a month and supports a wife and three young children, was represented by lawyer Farazalila Fauzi from the National Legal Aid Foundation.
According to the facts of the case, the pupil’s mother was at a night market at about 5.15 pm on the day of the incident when her son told her that Abdullah had kicked him in the face during a Kafa class at the school.
The kick caused an injury to the pupil’s gums. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Kafa is the abbreviation in Malay for Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain.

Title: Psychosis impaired teen’s understanding he was taking a life in Bandar Utama school murder, court says, rejecting months‑long planning claim
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 23 — The Shah Alam High Court rejected claims that the 16-year-old schoolgirl’s murder in Bandar Utama last year was planned for months, finding that the accused’s psychotic illness impaired his understanding of the act and that the alleged “plan” stemmed from his delusions.
In her full written grounds, Judge Adlin Abdul Majid said she could not accept that merely knowing he was pushing a knife into the deceased’s abdomen and that it would cause her to bleed was sufficient to establish that the accused understood the nature of the act.
She added that an accused who has knowledge of the mechanics but not of the reality of what he is doing cannot be said to know the nature of the act.
“The nature of an act of homicide is not exhausted by its physical character. It must include the fact that the object of the act is a living human being with an existence independent of the actor, and that what is being destroyed is a real life, in the real world, permanently,” she said.
Adlin noted that a psychiatric report prepared by Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony, director and senior consultant forensic psychiatrist at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, recorded that the accused, through immersion in video games, came to view all persons as “NPCs” — useless, monotonous and computer-controlled characters lacking independent thought.
“He applied that label to students and teachers at the school, to his own parents and to society as a whole.
She also said the report recorded that due to the multitude of intense psychotic symptoms, the accused was transported into a world of fiction and fantasy, detached from reality, in a parallel world inhabited only by himself and the deceased.
“DW2 (Dr Ian) described delusional atmosphere and delusional memory as primary delusions, which are rare and are indicative of extremely severe psychosis.
“A primary delusion is not a mistaken inference drawn from experience. It is a direct, unmediated alteration in the way reality itself presents.
“It cannot be reasoned with, because it is not the product of reasoning,” she said.
Nevertheless, Adlin said the most telling piece of evidence supporting this finding is that the accused did not grasp the finality of death and believed that the deceased would be reincarnated.
“From this evidence, I am satisfied that the child’s psychotic illness had, at the material time, deprived him of the capacity to comprehend that he was taking the life of a living person, as opposed to enacting a fantasy upon an object of his own delusional construction.
“Accordingly, I am satisfied on a balance of probabilities that at the time of the Incident, by reason of unsoundness of mind, the child did not have the capacity to know the nature of the act he committed,” she said.
Prosecution challenge
On the prosecution’s argument that the accused’s delusions were simply a reason or motive for the killing, Adlin disagreed, finding that the delusions did not just give him a reason to kill but affected his ability to understand that what he was doing was wrong.
“Rather, it is the delusions themselves, and the associated dissociative state, that deprived him of that appreciation,” she said.
She also rejected the prosecution’s contention that the accused’s months-long planning showed he had the ability to organise, sequence and adjust his actions.
“The evidence establishes that every material element of the ‘plan’ relied upon by the prosecution was itself generated within and by the delusional system, rather than by rational, self-interested deliberation directed at a real-world objective.
“The target was selected not by reason of any relationship, dispute, or rational motive, but by an erotomanic delusion attaching to a girl whom, as the evidence established, the child had never once spoken to or otherwise contacted,” she said.
Adlin noted that the original date of the planned killing was also fixed to coincide with the anniversary of an atrocity committed 25 years earlier in another country by two young men whom the accused had come to identify with through his illness.
In addition, writings on the knives were made at the instruction of a hallucinated voice he attributed to Dylan Klebold, while the clothing was assembled piece by piece to replicate that worn by the Columbine High School shooting perpetrators.
None of this, the judge said, reflected the conduct of a rational, self-interested actor but rather the enactment of a delusional identification that had consumed the child’s inner life.
She also said the accused’s failure to plan an escape, dispose of evidence, or evade capture after the incident was more consistent with, and positively explained by, the psychiatric evidence that his actions were driven by psychosis.
“A plan which was meticulously prepared as to matters of costume and inscription, yet totally indifferent to detection, risk and escape, is not, in my assessment, the plan of a rational, guilt-aware mind,” she said.
She also dismissed the prosecution’s argument that the accused’s stalking of the deceased showed focused, deliberate and non-random targeting inconsistent with a psychotic attack.
“Based on DW2’s unrebutted evidence, sustained and specific attention to a single object of fixation, over a period exceeding a year and in the complete absence of any real encounter or exchange between the child and the deceased, is a recognised feature of erotomanic delusion,” she said.
Adlin also accepted Dr Ian’s evidence that a person can experience severe psychosis while still being able to carry out simple, everyday tasks, rejecting the prosecution’s argument that the accused’s normal behaviour on the day showed he was aware of what was happening around him and therefore could not be considered legally insane.
She also rejected the prosecution’s argument that the severity and repeated nature of the attack showed the accused deliberately intended to kill the victim and ensure she had no chance of being rescued.
“From DW2’s evidence, the violence inflicted on the deceased went well beyond what was needed to cause death, and served no purpose.
“This fact together with the disparity between the number of injuries and the child’s recollection of them supports the finding that the child’s mind was overwhelmed by psychosis and dissociation at the time of the incident.
She said the same detached state continued after the incident, with the accused seen calmly walking through the chaos of alarms and screams, stopping to retrieve and drink from his water bottle while still holding the knife.
“This event corroborates, rather than undermines, the account of dissociation during the act itself,” she said.
Untimely and tragic death
Adlin also said that her decision to acquit and discharge the accused did not make the deceased’s death any less devastating or real because it was caused by illness rather than malice.
She stressed that despite finding the accused committed the act but was not criminally responsible due to unsoundness of mind, the decision should not diminish the value of the deceased’s life or cause anyone to forget her.
“This is not a finding that the act did not happen, or that no one was responsible for it.
“It is a finding that the person who committed the act was at the time in the grip of a serious psychotic illness that had gone unrecognised and untreated for years, and that the law does not hold such a person criminally responsible for conduct he could not, at that moment, appreciate as wrong,” she said.
Noting that the deceased was a young student with close family and friends and a bright future ahead of her, Adlin said her untimely death was an immense and irreversible loss, stressing that her family’s grief was not diminished by the accused’s diagnosis and that the judgment did not ask them to see it that way.
Instead, Adlin said the case highlighted how far serious mental illness can progress in a child without being noticed by those around him, and how serious the consequences can be.
“Here, symptoms of a very early-onset and ultimately extremely severe psychotic illness were present from the age of nine, documented over five years in family accounts, school records and teachers’ observations, yet never once recognised as an illness.
“The signs were there: withdrawal, delusional thinking, a refusal to remove his mask, chronic lateness born of fear and hallucinated voices.
“They were read, understandably, as behavioural or disciplinary problems rather than as a medical emergency. The cost of that misreading has now been borne by two families,” she said.
She said if any good could come from the tragedy, it was for parents, schools, the courts and the wider public to better understand the signs and consequences of untreated mental illness in children.
“...So that symptoms are recognised and treated earlier, and never again permitted to progress unaddressed, to a point of such devastating consequence so that other families may be spared what both these families have suffered.
“It is in this spirit that this decision was made,” she said.

Title: Rosmah’s RM67.5m jewellery bill: No pause button, Court of Appeal rules
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 23 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has lost her latest bid to fully halt a RM67.5 million payment owed to Lebanese jeweller Global Royalty Trading SAL over dozens of missing jewellery pieces.
The Court of Appeal has dismissed her appeal against a High Court order for a conditional stay, meaning the sum must still be deposited into a stakeholder account within a month of the August 12 judgement,
The Edge
reported today.
“He can and is willing and able” to collect “every cent” of the judgement sum, the jeweller's lawyer Datuk David Gurupatham was quoted telling reporters outside the courtroom after the decision was announced.
The dispute traces back to a June High Court ruling by Judicial Commissioner Datuk Quay Chew Soon, which held Rosmah liable for 43 pieces of jewellery that went missing after a 2018 police raid.
Rosmah had wanted the payment paused entirely pending her main appeal, arguing her assets were tied up in 1Malaysia Development Bhd's (1MDB) separate US$350 million (RM1.6 billion) suit against her.
She had given an undertaking in June 2024 not to dispose of luxury goods worth about RM600 million linked to that 1MDB claim.
According to
The Edge
, David pushed back, telling the court the value of the 1MDB-linked assets had not been established and that ownership of the jewellery itself was still unverified.
“Unless [Rosmah] has been living on fresh air and the goodwill of the people,” he was quoted as saying, adding that a document showing just RM100,000 in a dormant Affin Bank account could not be treated as proof of her financial position.
A three-member bench led by Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril agreed there were no grounds for an unconditional stay, noting her 1MDB undertaking only covered a specific, agreed list of items — not her full asset picture.
The judges also pointed out the Attorney General's Chambers had not objected to the jeweller's application.
Of the 44 jewellery pieces originally involved, only one has been recovered and returned so far.
Rosmah's main appeal is set to be heard on March 25, 2027, and the Court of Appeal ordered her to pay RM30,000 in costs.

Title: Zero motions, zero Bills: Dewan Rakyat Speaker still waiting on no-confidence bid, PM term-limit, and AG-PP split
Article:
BANGI, Sept 23 — Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said he has yet to receive any motion of no confidence for the upcoming parliamentary sitting.
“Not even one (motion of no confidence) has been received. I have not heard anything about it,” he told reporters after officiating the ‘Negara Bangsa: Membina Jati Diri dan Identiti Nasional’ dialogue here today.
His remarks came after UMNO president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi challenged any party seeking to remove UMNO and Barisan Nasional (BN) from the Unity Government to formally do so by tabling a no-confidence motion in the Dewan Rakyat.
Johari also said he had yet to receive the proposed Bills on the separation of the roles of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor, as well as the Bill to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure.
“I was informed that there were plans for them, but I have yet to receive the papers. Usually, two weeks before the tabling, the Speaker will be informed. But so far, I have not received anything,” he said.
Earlier, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bill to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure was ready to be tabled in the upcoming parliamentary session.
According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar on the Parliament website, the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament will run for 37 days from Oct 5 to Dec 8, with Budget 2027 scheduled to be tabled on Oct 9. — Bernama

Title: Anwar courts Chinese industry leaders with eye on investments in chips, AI and robotics
Article:
SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — A roundtable discussion with industry leaders from 21 leading Chinese companies here focused on various high-impact sectors, including semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics, as Malaysia explores high-value strategic investments, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The discussion also touched on the potential of electric vehicles (EVs), battery materials, advanced optics, biotechnology, healthcare, specialty chemicals and advanced manufacturing.
“I also heard directly from industry players about their plans and aspirations, including the opportunities they see in Malaysia and the steps needed to realise these investments.
“The Madani Government will continue to facilitate quality investments that bring technology transfer, develop local talent, strengthen the participation of Malaysian companies and create more quality job opportunities,” he said in a post on X following the meeting.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said Malaysia has a strong foundation to continue developing as a high-value investment and manufacturing hub in the region, supported by a mature industrial ecosystem, skilled workforce, strategic location and strong supply chain networks.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook also participated in the discussion.
China has been Malaysia’s largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with bilateral trade reaching US$113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) from January to August this year.
Anwar arrived here on Tuesday for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou. — Bernama

Title: Three-day remand for two men as Sarawak police probe convenience store fire cases
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 23 — Two men aged 40 and 23 were remanded for three days by the Magistrates’ Court here today to assist investigations into a case of mischief by fire involving a convenience store along Jalan Green here.
Senior Court Registrar Syazwani Sajeli allowed the remand application after hearing submissions by investigating officer Insp Tan Chiang Fook and their counsel Daniel Ling.
The court ordered both suspects to be remanded for three days from Sept 23 to Sept 26 to assist investigations under Section 436 of the Penal Code.
It was reported that the incident occurred at the premises in Jalan Green, Sin Sin Park here at about 8.30pm on Sept 20.
The 40-year-old suspect was arrested at a premises in Sibu at about 2.40pm on Sept 22, while the other was arrested later the same day at about 9.30pm at a cafe along Jalan Nanas, Sarikei.
The case is one of two incidents of mischief by fire reported in Kuching and Sri Aman on Sept 20, involving premises belonging to the same convenience store chain.
Three suspects have been arrested and remanded to assist investigations into both incidents. — The Borneo Post

Title: Haze eases in Lubok Antu, but Kanowit air remains ‘very unhealthy’ at midday
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 23 — Lubok Antu moved out of the very unhealthy category by noon today after its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading dropped from 205 at 8am to 195.
The improvement left Kanowit as the only station in Sarawak recording a very unhealthy reading at noon, with its API at 208, down from 244 at 8am.
Despite the improvement, Lubok Antu remained in the unhealthy category, according to the latest API readings from the Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB) Status for Sarawak.
Most monitoring stations across Sarawak also remained in the unhealthy category at noon, with readings ranging from 105 to 195.
Serian recorded the highest unhealthy reading at 186, followed by Sri Aman at 180, Betong at 178, Belaga at 174 and Samarahan at 173.
Kuching registered 179, while Bintulu was at 170, Sarikei 168, Sibu 167, Miri 161 and Samalaju 162.
Other readings included ILP Miri at 158, Tebedu 159, Mukah and Limbang 153 each, Lundu 128, Lawas 129 and Kapit 121.
Bario was the only station outside the unhealthy and very unhealthy categories, recording a moderate reading of 74 at noon compared with 33 at 8am.
Under the API classification, readings of 0–50 are considered good, 51–100 moderate, 101–200 unhealthy and 201–300 very unhealthy. — The Borneo Post

Title: ‘Your country is proud of you’, Anwar tells 22 Malaysians competing at WorldSkills Shanghai
Article:
SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hailed Malaysia’s 22 young competitors at the 48th WorldSkills Competition here as the country’s pride, stressing that skilled workers are indispensable to a modern, technology-driven economy.
“You have spent years practising something difficult until you could do it well. Whatever the result this week, your country is proud of you.
“Your participation here lets Malaysia test itself against the best in the world. It shows us how our standards compare and where we can improve,” he said at the plenary session of the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 Conference and Expo here today.
Malaysia is represented by 22 young competitors across 21 skill areas at the competition, which brings together about 1,400 young professionals from more than 65 countries and regions, marking the country’s continued participation in the event since 1995.
Touching on youth’s role in the economy, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said young skilled workers play a crucial role in keeping modern economies running, even as machinery and software become increasingly sophisticated.
“A modern economy cannot function without the technicians who keep a semiconductor line running or an electric vehicle plant on schedule.
“The machinery may become more sophisticated. The software may become more intelligent. But somebody still has to understand how it works and know what to do when it does not,” he said.
Anwar said young people would be drawn to technical and skilled professions if they could see clear prospects for career advancement and better livelihoods.
“Our task is to make sure that it leads somewhere worth going: to skilled work and good incomes. Skill of that depth is built slowly,” said the Prime Minister.
Citing an old Chinese saying that it takes 10 years to grow a tree but 100 years to cultivate a person, Anwar said the energy and dynamism of young people were pivotal to economic progress, and that society must move beyond viewing youth merely as contributors to material and economic advancement.
“There isn’t any doubt that the energy and vibrancy of young people contributes substantively to high productivity in this pursuit of material wealth,” he said.
Anwar said young people also make significant contributions to society, including by championing social justice, addressing wealth inequalities and pushing for poverty eradication.
“Thanks to the young people, the drive to foster societal improvement, demand for social justice, ending the inequities of wealth, and pushing for poverty eradication. These are paramount.
“A country can attract capital. It can acquire technology. It still needs people who know how to make that technology work and make it better,” said Anwar.
The prime minister arrived here on Tuesday for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou. — Bernama

Title: Overseas markets key to growing Malaysia’s oil and gas services sector in next three years, says economy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The government expects the oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) sector to increase its output and revenue in the next two to three years through expansion into overseas markets, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
Speaking to reporters today, he said greater international market participation would strengthen the sector’s revenue streams while improving the resilience of Malaysian OGSE companies against economic and industry shocks.
“When we talk about the potential in terms of the international oil and gas market, developing countries will be a good place for us to venture into and that is why in terms of our planning through this international market access programme, Timor-Leste will be among the destinations that we will go into.
“But definitely the groundwork must be done through Malaysia Petroleum Resources Corporation (MPRC) to build up the rapport and provide the mechanism and really to ease the process,” said Akmal Nasrullah after the preview of MPRC International Market Access Programme’s (IMAP) Privet OGSE Turkmenistan here today.
Also present were Ministry of Economy secretary general, Datuk Seri Nor Azmie Diron and MPRC president/chief executive officer Mohd Yazid Ja’afar.
In 2023, the sector generated about RM79 billion in gross output and RM39.4 billion in value added to the economy.
As part of the effort, 14 Malaysian OGSE companies will participate in an upcoming mission to Turkmenistan in October to assess opportunities in the Central Asian country’s oil and gas industry.
Akmal Nasrullah said the companies were selected based on their capabilities, credibility and interest in exploring opportunities in Turkmenistan.
The initiative is being undertaken by the MPRC under IMAP, which is aimed at helping Malaysian OGSE companies diversify and expand their international market presence.
Akmal Nasrullah said international diversification was important to strengthen the resilience of Malaysian OGSE companies and reduce their reliance on the domestic market.
Malaysia has about 2,894 OGSE companies, of which 91 per cent are micro, small and medium-sized companies.
He said the government, therefore, wanted to help these companies scale up their capabilities, including by enabling them to tap opportunities abroad. — Bernama

Title: Teen accused in Bandar Utama school killing diagnosed with early-onset schizophrenia and viewed others as ‘non-player characters’
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 23 — The 15-year-old boy who killed his female schoolmate at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year had come to view the victim and those around him as “NPCs”, the Shah Alam High Court was told.
In gaming terminology, an NPC — or non‑player character — refers to background characters controlled by the game rather than by a human player, and the term is sometimes used online to imply that a person lacks agency or individuality.
In her full grounds of judgment, Judge Adlin Abdul Majid said this was disclosed in a psychiatric report prepared by Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony, the director and senior consultant forensic psychiatrist at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta.
In disclosing his findings, Dr Ian highlighted the existence of a “
Death Note
” journal on the accused’s mobile phone, in which he repeatedly referred to the deceased while chronicling the disturbing and psychotic thoughts in his mind.
Death Note
is a Japanese anime and manga series centred on a student who discovers a supernatural notebook that allows him to kill anyone by writing their name, and the character Kira — whom the accused identified with — is portrayed as a vigilante who believes he has the authority to judge and eliminate others.
The journal, written in Mandarin, contained accounts of his symptoms six months before the murder.
“The entries show persecutory beliefs that classmates were conspiring against him and deserved to die, a wish for mass casualties, and a conviction that others would lie to the police to make him appear at fault.
“They show his dehumanisation of those around him, most starkly in his adoption of the term NPC to describe his schoolmates as subhuman, valueless game objects.
“They show a grandiose delusion of having become Kira, a godlike figure entitled to judge and eliminate others, and open identification with Eric Harris, Dylan Klebold and other mass killers as role models and (in his own words) as gods,” she said in her grounds.
Adlin said the entries further showed the evolution of his fixation on the deceased, from professed love to an intention to take her with him in death, alongside pervasive suicidal thoughts, profound loneliness and a belief that his self-worth was entirely tied to his physical appearance.
Psychiatric report findings
The psychiatric report also noted a strong family history of mental illness, including an institutionalised aunt, a mentally disordered paternal grand-uncle and two affected sons, as well as a family member treated for depression.
Dr Ian further said that the child’s situation worsened over the years as he was exposed to the internet, video games and anime.
The report said that from around 2020, when the child was nine and during the Covid-19 movement control period, his family and later teachers observed a gradual change in his behaviour, with him becoming withdrawn, isolating himself in his room and refusing to communicate with his family.
“He also developed a persistent belief that he was physically unattractive and that other students were laughing at and talking about him.
“He began wearing a face mask at all times, even after public health requirements had ended, refusing to remove it to eat or drink at school.”
Outside home, he became highly anxious and believed people were observing him, which the report described as paranoid delusions.
The psychiatric report identified a further evolution of psychotic symptoms in 2023, when he became suspicious that CCTV cameras had been secretly installed in his home and believed he was being watched by ‘the eye’ of a technician who had repaired the system.
The report described this as a paranoid delusion, reinforced by his perception of a red light in his room, which was recorded as a visual hallucination.
“He later became convinced that his parents had covertly installed cameras in his room and bathroom.
“By early 2025, the belief had extended to his school, where he believed the security guard and certain teachers were secretly monitoring him via CCTV, including while he was in the school washroom,” the report added.
Dr Ian also said the accused began developing an interest in school shooters and serial killers, while from around August 2024, he developed an infatuation with the deceased.
Seven months before the murder, Dr Ian noted that the accused began experiencing auditory hallucinations in the form of a voice he attributed to Dylan Klebold, speaking to him in Mandarin and instructing him to kill the deceased.
Around the same period, the accused also began identifying with Light Yagami, or Kira, the god-like vigilante from
Death Note
.
“Taken as a whole, I accept that this chronology reflects a serious and longstanding psychotic illness that developed and worsened progressively over several years.
“By the time of the incident, the child was in the grip of an active psychosis, marked by delusions directed at the deceased and a commanding hallucinated voice instructing him to kill her,” Adlin said.
She said Dr Ian’s testimony rejected the suggestion that the accused had feigned his symptoms, with the journal entries confirming that the psychotic beliefs described in the psychiatric report were not constructed for the trial but were genuinely present in the boy’s mind in the period leading up to the incident.
Adlin said that three weeks after being prescribed antipsychotic medication, Dr Ian testified that the accused’s hallucinations had ceased and his delusions had begun to dissolve, while he also began engaging warmly with his family in a manner not seen for years.
In fact, the illness’s severity was well documented, with Dr Ian stating that the accused had experienced a wide range of psychiatric symptoms for about five years without receiving medical treatment by the time the offence occurred, including severe and debilitating psychotic symptoms in the form of hallucinations and delusions.
“Based on the evidence set out in the psychiatric report, DW2 (Dr Ian) diagnosed the child with schizophrenia, of very early onset (before the age of 13) with psychopathic and sadistic traits.
During cross-examination, Adlin said DW2 drew an important distinction between hallucinations and delusions, explaining that hallucinations are intermittent and come and go, whereas delusions are fixed and continuously present.
“On this basis, the delusional system was not something that came upon the child occasionally. It was present throughout, including during the incident,” she said.
Adlin also noted that DW2 explained the clinical significance of the accused having remained untreated for five years, noting that this period, known as the duration of untreated psychosis (DUP), is measured from the onset of symptoms to the start of medication.
“The Malaysian mean DUP is 28.7 months, compared with approximately 60 months in the child’s case.
“DW2 then elaborated that untreated psychosis does not remain static — it becomes more elaborate over time, and the longer it goes unchallenged, the more internally logical it becomes to the person experiencing it, and the more resistant to correction.
“As such, by the time of the incident, the child’s reality testing was impaired to the point that the world he perceived was not the world the rest of us live in,” she said.

Title: New Beijing-Kota Kinabalu route on the cards as China Eastern eyes more Sabah flights
Article:
SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — China Eastern Airlines plans to increase its Shanghai-Kota Kinabalu services to double or even triple daily flights, while exploring a direct Beijing-Kota Kinabalu route.
The plans were discussed during a courtesy visit by Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin to China Eastern Airlines’ office in Shanghai on Tuesday, where he met Senior Vice President of Marketing and Sales Yang Chun Fei.
Also present were Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Ministry Permanent Secretary Datuk Josie Lai and representatives from the Sabah Tourism Board.
Jafry welcomed the plans, saying stronger direct air connectivity was crucial as Sabah prepared for Visit Sabah 2027, adding that increased frequencies would provide greater capacity and flexibility for travellers.
He said a direct Beijing-Kota Kinabalu route would open another major gateway and further strengthen Sabah’s connectivity with China, which recorded 578,681 arrivals in the first eight months of 2026, up 21.6 per cent from the same period last year, while China Eastern operated up to three daily Shanghai-Kota Kinabalu services during the 2026 peak summer travel period. — Daily Express
Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin (centre) receives a memento from China Eastern Airlines (Sales & Marketing) Senior Vice President Yang Chun Fei (left). — Daily Express pic
